newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end down; index at new 3-yr closing low.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end down; index at new 3-yr closing low.

text.p: Stocks ended at a new three-year closing low on Friday after widely fluctuating as selling for repayment of margin loans took its toll, brokers said.
But the sharp falls in mid-afternoon have been mostly recouped towards the close by bargain-hunting, they said.
The composite stock index provisionally closed at 689.07, down 0.37 of a point on the day. It was well off an intra-day low of 677.64.
"Many investors, especially individuals dumped shares as the market's slump has continued longer than expected," said Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities.
Decliners far outpaced advancers by 690 to 231.
An early rebound, sparked by bargain hunting following sharp falls on Thursday, was soon reversed as selling spread wide through the rest of the day.
Volume totalled 26.14 million shares, up slightly from 25.89 million on Thursday.
The KOSPI-200 index bucked the overall market trend, ending 0.36 of a point higher at 70.27.
Brokers said stocks making up the KOSPI-200 index attracted buying interest after these stocks fell sharply on Thursday due to institutional selling.
Brokers said institutions heavily sold the KOSPI-200 stocks to maximise gains on the December futures contract, which was settled on Thursday.
Daewoo Corp rose 350 won to 6,300 and Kyungnam Energy was up 1,500 won to 56,500.
Blue chip rebounds also supported the composite index. Korea Mobile Telecom gained 23,500 won to 441,500 and Dacom Corp added 7,000 won to 109,000.
